newsitem.title: POLAND: FOCUS-Polish mkts unruffled by fin minister change.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Polish mkts unruffled by fin minister change.

text.p: Polish financial markets on Tuesday reacted coolly to the departure of Finance Minister Grzegorz Kolodko, expecting no major changes in economic policy from his replacement Marek Belka, traders said.
But they said investors might stay cautious for some time until they become more familiar with the new finance chief.
Belka, an independent economist and hitherto adviser to the Polish President, said he would continue a policy of macro-economic consolidation, curbing inflation and running a tight budget.
Analysts said Belka was relatively unknown to investors and they would await reassurance that he would get his way in the tough world of politics.
"Polish markets and foreign investors want to see what Belka will do, because he is relatively unknown," said Wojciech Kowalczyk, a senior dealer at Bank Handlowy SA.
Bankers said the financial markets would be particularily keen to see that Belka keeps a tight grip on government spending and inflation in the election year.
"We will see if the government loosens its financial discipline with the arrival of the new Finance Minister," said one analyst at a foreign company here.

Warsaw stocks inched up 0.1 percent to 16,525.2 points of the main WIG index, extending a recent bull run and mixed post-fixing trade signalled investors were was not clear about its near-term direction.

The zloty was calm in morning trade, holding flat against the basket of currencies with no large upward or downward pressure, while T-bill yields inched up on liquidity swings rather than the news of Kolodko's resignation.

Analysts said that with the 1997 budget ready any radical shift in economic policy was highly unlikely but foreign players in particular would need some time to digest the news and were likely to keep sidelined for some time.

"I think people will wait and see if there is a change to any policies...Poland is...in very good shape right now and Kolodko was seen as doing a very good job recently," Stephen Pettyfer, analyst at Merrill Lynch in London said.
"But I don't think the market expects the new appointment, given his background, to make a great change."
Some analysts said the markets also should have already discounted recent frictions within the government especially after Kolodko clashed with his cabinet colleagues over duties on grain imports.
Polish discount Brady bonds were flat around 98.25/98.50, signalling that foreign investors were relaxed over Kolodko's dismissal and remained generally bullish on Poland.
